note: The authoritative bundle and build lifecycles. NOT a JSON Schema and deliberately not under schemas/ — a document at a schema path is loadable as a schema whether or not it is one, and one that is not turns into a validator accepting everything (review finding dd46cac-F1). Nothing validates against this file; T6's tables, the coordinator and the admin API are written from it, and dev/schema-fixture-check.py checks it is internally consistent. The transitions live here and only here: WORKPLAN-BUNDLES.md describes why they are what they are and does not restate them, because restating a policy in two places is what produced finding d4f5baf-F1.

identifiers.form: Lower-case canonical UUID, server-generated. A publisher never supplies one and never sees one reused.
identifiers.bundle_id: One accepted upload and its immutable bytes. Survives every build that reads it, including retries.
identifiers.build_id: One execution ATTEMPT. Not a bundle hash, not a content version, not a worker or container id. A retry is a new build_id carrying retry_of, reusing the same validated bundle.
identifiers.version_id: One content_version row, created only on success. Distinct from the display version number, which is the n in a spec id's --v<n>.
identifiers.rendition_id: One set of output files for a version. Reserved by spine #2, produced by #5/#6.
identifiers.idempotency_key: Caller-supplied, scoped to one content item. Its job is to stop an HTTP retry becoming a second execution attempt; it is not an identifier of anything and never appears in an object key or an image tag.
identifiers.lease_generation: Monotonic per build. A worker that loses its lease is fenced: updates and publication from the old generation are refused rather than merged.

bundle.description: What happens to an upload. Ends at VALIDATED, which is durable and reusable: a bundle is built any number of times without changing state.

states.UPLOADING: Bytes are arriving. No receipt is committed, so nothing may read it.
states.VALIDATING: Bytes are complete and the receipt is committed. Schema, semantic rules S1-S9, bounded extraction and S10-S11 run here.
states.VALIDATED: Immutable and buildable. The only state a build may start from.
states.REJECTED: Failed a named rule. Retained for diagnosis under the failed-artifact policy; never becomes VALIDATED.

transitions.trigger: all bytes received and receipt committed
upload abandoned past its deadline, or a transport-level limit exceeded

bundle.upload_admissible_rationale: The states in which raw bytes may still be accepted: exactly those with NO committed receipt. UPLOADING is the only one. VALIDATING is not terminal and is not admissible either -- its own description says the bytes are complete and the receipt is committed -- which is why this is declared rather than derived from terminality. A checker that used 'not terminal' as a synonym for 'still writable' accepted VALIDATING and would have permitted exactly the committed-byte replacement the transport forbids (finding 2b01e24-F1).

build.description: One execution attempt. Every terminal state is final: no terminal attempt returns to running, and a retry is a different build_id.

states.QUEUED: Admitted, not yet leased to a worker. Cancellation here is immediate because nothing is running.
states.RUNNING: A worker holds the lease and is executing untrusted code.
states.PUBLISHING: The image is being pushed and the version transaction prepared. Operator cancellation is REFUSED here: the push may already have produced a digest, and a cancel that races publication is how an image exists with no row describing it. A DEADLINE is not refused -- the worker's lifetime bound covers this phase too, because a push or a verification can stall after the build itself has finished.
states.SUCCEEDED: Image published and verified, logs persisted, exactly one content_version inserted and linked. Does not activate anything.
states.FAILED: A build step failed, or publication could not be completed. No version exists.
states.CANCELLED: An operator stopped it, and the worker is confirmed stopped.
states.TIMED_OUT: The attempt exceeded its configured deadline and was stopped.
states.INTERRUPTED: The platform lost the attempt — worker death, lease loss, or a restart across it. Distinct from FAILED because nothing is known about how far it got, which is why its artifacts are retained rather than assumed absent.

transitions.trigger: admission state lost before a lease was taken
cancel requested and the whole worker confirmed stopped
worker died or the lease was lost
image verified, logs persisted and the version transaction committed
push, verification or the version transaction failed
the platform lost the attempt mid-publication; reconciliation decides what exists

configured deadline exceeded during push or verification; the worker is stopped first, late completion is fenced by lease generation, and any image already pushed becomes an unreferenced artifact for the collector

invariants: A content_version row exists only for a SUCCEEDED build, and exactly one per success.
No state transition activates anything. Activation is a separate, explicit, content-scoped operation.
Retention clocks for a build start when it reaches a terminal state, never at creation.
A terminal state is final. Retrying produces a new build_id with retry_of set, not a reopened attempt.

Cancellation is refused once PUBLISHING has begun. Recovery is deleting the CONTENT, which is the only delete the admin API has; there is no version-delete endpoint and this rationale does not create one.

A deadline that expires during PUBLISHING produces TIMED_OUT and never a late SUCCEEDED: the version transaction is fenced by lease generation, so a worker that finishes after its deadline cannot insert a content_version.
